newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican peso nosedives on risk worries, U.S. factors.
newsitem.headline: Mexican peso nosedives on risk worries, U.S. factors.

text.p: The Mexican peso took a nosedive Friday and stock prices fell sharply as investors scrambled to buy dollars, attracted by higher U.S. interest rates and concerned about political risk in Mexico, traders said.
"There is demand (for dollars) from everywhere. People are taking them at almost any level," said one dealer.

"Foreigners are saying that Mexico is pure risk while the (U.S. 30-year Treasury) bond is going up and looks like an attractive alternative to get out of the Mexican market," another foreign exchange trader said.

The same-day peso opened 11.30 centavos weaker at 7.60/7.62 per dollar while in 24-hour and 48-hour contracts it was 11.45 centavos and 9.75 centavos weaker at 7.60/7.6375 per dollar and 7.60/7.6375 per dollar respectively.
The 30-year U.S. Treasury bond yield rose sharply to 7.13 percent in response to stronger-than-expected U.S. economic data.
The main Mexican stock market index was down about 50 points, or 1.53 percent, in early trading.
